I'm a bit rusty on my element classifications, but I remember that metals are elements that are good conductors of electricity and have a shiny, metallic appearance. They usually have a positive charge when they lose electrons.

Looking at option A: iodine, iron, nickel. I know iron and nickel are metals because they are commonly used in construction and are known for their metallic properties. But iodine, isn't that a non-metal? I think non-metals are elements like carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, which are on the right side of the periodic table. Iodine is actually a halogen, which is a non-metal. So option A has a non-metal, so it's not all metals.

Option B: helium, carbon, gold. Helium is a noble gas, so it's a non-metal. Carbon is definitely a non-metal; it's in the same group as silicon and is used in things like diamonds and graphite. Gold is a metal, but since there are non-metals in this set, it's out.

Option C: sodium, chromium, copper. Sodium is an alkali metal, which means it's a metal. Chromium is a transition metal, so that's a metal too. Copper is also a metal, used in wires and coins. So all three are metals, which makes this option a good candidate.

Option D: phosphorus, nitrogen, oxygen. All of these are non-metals. Phosphorus and nitrogen are in the nitrogen family, and oxygen is a diatomic non-metal. So this set has no metals at all.

Chromium is known for being hard and used in stainless steel. Copper is a soft, reddish-brown metal. Yeah, all metals. The other options either have non-metals or a mix, so C is the only one with all metals.
